style.opening: set of 4 solid black silhouettes of the same WWII infantry soldier in four poses, 2×2 grid, evenly spaced on a flat pure white background, each figure whole from head to boots, centered in an equal square cell, the same height and the same build in every cell.
style.style: full side profile facing right, bareheaded with a plain round head (no helmet, no cap), empty hands placed where the weapon would be held but no weapon drawn, plain trousers and a plain tunic with no visible kit, solid flat black fill, crisp clean outline, no interior lines, strong readable outline at small size, stocky toy soldier proportions: broad shoulders, thick arms and legs, a slightly large head, and bold hands
style.parameters: --no helmet, hat, cap, rifle, gun, weapon, bayonet, pack, text, ground, floor, shadow, gradient, scenery, color --style raw --stylize 50 --ar 1:1
style.singleOpening: a single solid black silhouette of a WWII infantry soldier on a flat pure white background, the whole figure from head to boots, centered with even margins, one figure only.

briefs.label: Squad: standing rifleman
briefs.brief: an infantryman advancing at a steady walk, mid-stride, torso upright and leaning slightly forward, rear hand low at the hip and front hand forward at chest height as if carrying a rifle at the ready
briefs.meaning: Squads and half-squads, front face; repeated two or three times for size (A1.2).

briefs.label: Crew: kneeling
briefs.brief: a gun crewman kneeling on one knee, torso upright, both hands forward at waist height as if working a gun breech
briefs.meaning: Crews (A1.123, A21), so a crew reads apart from a half-squad.

briefs.label: Leader: pointing
briefs.brief: an officer standing upright, front arm fully extended pointing forward, rear hand low at the hip as if holding a submachine gun

briefs.label: Hero: charging
briefs.brief: a soldier charging forward at a run, body leaning hard forward, rear arm drawn back, front arm forward as if about to throw a grenade

briefs.label: Wounded leader or hero
briefs.brief: a wounded soldier standing hunched, one hand pressed to his side, the other arm hanging low, knees slightly bent
briefs.meaning: The wounded face of a leader or a hero (A15.2, A17).

briefs.label: Broken: falling back
briefs.brief: a soldier crouching low and turning away to the left, hunched over, head down, one arm raised over the head for cover
briefs.meaning: The broken face of any personnel (A10).

briefs.label: Pinned: prone
briefs.brief: a soldier lying flat on his stomach, head toward the right raised slightly, elbows on the ground, hands forward as if aiming a rifle

briefs.label: Berserk: bayonet charge
briefs.brief: a soldier in a wild sprint, legs in a long stride, both hands thrust forward low as if driving a bayonet, head forward, shouting

briefs.label: Prisoner: hands raised
briefs.brief: a prisoner standing upright, both hands raised above the head, palms open, weaponless
briefs.meaning: A captured unit in a Guard's custody (A20.5).
